findings: The frozen repository context contains four equivalent source phrasings and three current Question IDs for the direct String/StringBuilder/StringBuffer comparison; the candidate answers that exact concept without drifting into unrelated pool, layout or microbenchmark material.

The Java SE 26 String, StringBuilder and StringBuffer APIs support the candidate's mutability and synchronization distinctions, capacity/building model and practical selection rule; the JLS 26 concatenation section supports the explicit boundary that source-level String '+' does not mandate one fixed builder lowering strategy.

The comparison is organized on common dimensions rather than three disconnected definitions: mutability, synchronization contract, performance mechanism and selection conditions are contrasted directly, with the important boundary that thread-confined StringBuilder use is normal even inside a multithreaded program.

It also avoids the incorrect claim that String immutability follows merely from the class being final.

Performance claims are appropriately bounded: the answer explains mutable-capacity reuse and synchronization cost structurally while refusing universal speed multipliers, allocation counts or a fixed javac lowering strategy across JDK versions and workloads.

The project-experience section does not fabricate production results or personal ownership; it is framed as a practical mapping based on lifecycle and ownership, consistent with the repository no-fabrication rule.

The one-minute section has five concise comparison points, the three-minute section adds mechanism and selection detail rather than repeating the summary, and the six source-specific followups cover immutability, thread confinement, compound atomicity, selection, concatenation lowering and capacity tuning.
